newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING said eyeing U.S. buy in short term.
newsitem.headline: ING said eyeing U.S. buy in short term.

text.p: ING Groep NV (ING) executive board chairman Aad Jacobs told analysts last week that ING hopes to make a life insurance acquisition in the United States in the near future, analysts said on Monday.
They said Jacobs told a briefing on the Dutch group's first quarter results last Thursday that ING was talking to several U.S. life insurers but he declined to identify them.
"He gave the impression he hopes to conclude it pretty soon," said HSBC Van Meer James Capel analyst Ton Gietman.
Analysts have previously estimated that ING could afford to spend 7-8 billion guilders on an acquisition.
ING spokeswoman Manel Vrijenhoek repeated ING's previous statement that it was talking with potential targets.
"Of course we are talking to some of them," she told Reuters, but declined to provide more details.
Gietman said ING would wait until after its New York Stock Exchange listing on June 13 to expand in the United States as, after that date, it could offer its own equity to finance any acquisition.
Only U.S. listed shares can be used when equity is involved in an acquisition in the United States.
"He (Jacobs) hopes that in the very near future, he can come out with something," Kempen and Co analyst Hans Pluijgers said.

Jean-Paul van Bavel of F van Lanschot Bankiers said he hoped ING would make another large purchase in the foreseeable future as its equity reserves were "piling up", bolstered by reinvestment of dividends and conversion of warrants.
"It's getting too much. They have to do something with it," he said.
Heinie Hakker of BZW said ING had told analysts it was convinced "something will come out in the near future".
"But they also indicated they're not in far-reaching negotiations," he said, adding that it could be six months to a year before the Dutch group made its move.
